neighbours.label: philosophical logic and epistemology argument: laws, principles and foundations of belief or inference
fire: According to Leibniz, the principle of identity of indiscernibles rules out two identical things.
Hume argued that inductive inference cannot be justified without circularity.
Coherentists reply that beliefs are justified only by other beliefs in a web.
Kant called such judgments synthetic a priori: necessary yet informative.
The law of excluded middle says every proposition is either true or false.
Plato held that universal forms exist apart from particular objects.
A valid syllogism guarantees the conclusion if both premises are true.
Skeptics insist that no belief is certain unless it rests on indubitable grounds.
quiet: According to Leibniz's letters, he spent many years working in Hanover.
Hume worked as a librarian in Edinburgh and wrote a history of England.
Historians reply that the treaty was signed only after long delays.
Kant rarely travelled far from Königsberg during his long life.
The law requires every company to file its accounts by March.
Plato founded the Academy in Athens, which lasted for centuries.
A good recipe tells you the oven temperature and the baking time.
Tourists insist that no visit to Rome is complete without the Forum.
